notes: Every squad has been rebuilt from the confirmed 2026/27 roster. Names use surnames or the FPL-style web_name so the live-matcher works. Tier placement (best / first / sub / youth) is my editorial call based on 25/26 form and expected 26/27 role — feel free to reshuffle.

scoreMethodology.formula: clamp(tier_anchor + star_boost + output_boost + role_mod + team_bonus + variance, 0.10, 5.00)

components.star_boost: Editorial adjustment per named player (±1.5 for top stars)
components.output_boost: Real 25/26 statistical output — 0.11 × goals for scorers, 0.11 × clean sheets for GKs
components.variance: Deterministic ±0.14 wobble by name-hash for uniqueness

scoreMethodology.notes: Formula-based estimate. FBref blocks scraping so true WOWY (with-or-without-you) analytics were not accessible. Verified against Wikipedia 25/26 top scorers + clean sheets.
scoreMethodology.bestTierPrinciple: 'Best' (anchor 5.0) goes to the player whose season-long availability and role centrality make them hardest to replace -- proven full-season minutes and defensive/attacking centrality outrank reputation or transfer fee alone. Reassessed 11 Aug 2026: Liverpool's Best is now van Dijk (31 PL apps, captain, defensive lynchpin in 2025/26) rather than Wirtz (2,388 mins, 5G/3A in a partial season) -- durability was the deciding factor.

normalization.reason: Ensures WIscore is directly comparable club-to-club (fair league-table logic).

squadRules.basis: FPL price (against league-wide position bands) 40% + total points (relative to the club leader) 60%. First choice is a valid XI: 1 GK, 4+ DEF, 3+ MID, 1+ FWD. First sub is a 9-man matchday bench including the back-up keeper. Flagged players are credited with value-expected points so an injury does not demote them.
squadRules.source: FPL squad lists, 13 Oct 2026 (transfer window closed)
